ai.title: Terminal detection expanded with Zed, Tabby, Mintty, Konsole, GNOME
ai.summary: The CLI's ad client context now classifies additional Linux and Windows terminals by reading their environment variables (KONSOLE_VERSION, GNOME_TERMINAL_SCREEN, VTE_VERSION, XTERM_VERSION, WT_SESSION, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR, ZED_TERM), and the common type vocabulary was extended to accept the new terminal and install-method enums. The detection is additive: a new out-of-vocabulary value drops the whole context rather than the single field, so clients and servers must both speak the new values, per a newly added warning in the schema file. A related refactor in ad-signals.ts replaced the raw-text extractor failedToolOutputText with shellFailureClassOf, which returns a classified error class instead of text, and resets lastErrorClass to 'none' on each turn start so stale errors do not ride later turns.
ai.evidence: Three files changed: cli/src/ads/ad-client-context.ts adds terminal detection for zed, tabby, mintty, conemu, windows_console, gnome_terminal, konsole, vte, xterm, foot and konsole via new environment variable reads (KONSOLE_VERSION, KONSOLE_DBUS_SESSION, GNOME_TERMINAL_SCREEN, GNOME_TERMINAL_SERVICE, VTE_VERSION, XTERM_VERSION, WT_SESSION, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR, ZED_TERM); common/src/types/ad-client-context.ts adds the corresponding terminal enum values plus 'bunx' to INSTALL_METHODS and documents that vocabularies are additive-only (one out-of-range value drops the whole context); cli/src/ads/ad-signals.ts renames failedToolOutputText to shellFailureClassOf, which now returns an error class directly instead of raw text, and resets lastErrorClass to 'none' at each turn start.

eli5.text: The testing system that compares two AI coding helpers against each other has gotten stricter and more resilient. When an AI is being graded on a coding task, the grader now breaks the AI's work into smaller pieces and prioritizes the most relevant parts first, so large changes don't overwhelm it. If the grading AI fails to respond once, the system now automatically retries instead of giving up. The grading prompt can also be resumed if a long run gets interrupted, letting it skip tasks that already finished. This is an internal quality-control tool for the Freebuff team to measure how their AI assistants perform, so everyday users won't notice anything different, but it means their test results will be more reliable and complete.

ai.title: CLI ad engagement adds checkpoint and late-click merge records
ai.summary: The CLI ad engagement registry gains checkpoints and late-click merge handling in `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`: a live impression now emits a checkpoint via `checkpoint()` (the record so far, no exit) when a transcript card leaves the viewport after being seen, or after `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS` of exposure, whichever comes first, and a redraw of an already-flushed impression gets a click-only tracker that sends only `{ impUrl, click }` plus `postClick` so a late click still reaches the original record without overwriting the first click's features (the count grows instead). The `PartnerAdRow` component in `cli/src/components/partner-ad-line.tsx` is newly wired through `useAdEngagement` with placement: 'pinned', so partner rows now participate in that same registry alongside `AdCard`, and `cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts` calls `flushAdEngagementOnExit()` from the shared exit path so any record that survived on a transcript card is sent as `window_close` on quit. A new `AdEngagementPoster` in `use-ad-engagement.ts` sequences per-impression POSTs with the later write winning on the server merge, and `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS = 120_000` plus `MAX_CLICK_MEMO = 256` are the two new constants that gate the checkpoint timer and the clicked-impression memo.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`, `createEngagementRegistry.create` builds a click-only tracker via `createEngagementTracker({ clickOnly: { priorClick: clicks.get(impUrl) } })` when `mount` lands on an Impression already in finished, and the click-only `flush` path emits a `{ v, impUrl, click }` merge record through `sendLateClick`; `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS = 120_000` and `MAX_CLICK_MEMO = 256` bound the checkpoint timer and the clicked-impression memo respectively; in `cli/src/components/partner-ad-line.tsx` the new `PartnerAdRow` component calls `useAdEngagement(ad.impUrl, { placement: 'pinned', truncated: layoutTruncated([ [ad.title, getPartnerLineLayout(ad, width).title], ]) }) and wires onClick`/`onHover into that tracker; in cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts`, `createExitCliCleanly` pushes `Promise.resolve().then(deps.flushAdEngagement) into the exit cleanup list and the singleton supplies flushAdEngagement: () => flushAdEngagementOnExit() which calls live?.closeAll('window_close') followed by poster.settle()`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side consumer of the checkpoint or click-only merge records, nor the rollout of the engagement POST endpoint changes.

entries.title: CLI update: ad-adoption

ai.title: Ad engagement records out and adoption release on checkpoint
ai.summary: The engagement tracker now tracks a `recordOut` flag, marking it once the first record of any kind (a checkpoint, a late click, or a final flush) leaves for the impression, via a new `onRecordOut` callback threaded through `createEngagementTracker` and `createEngagementRegistry` and wired to `mainRecordSent` in the registry wiring. The adoption watcher's `status` check now releases a held `postClick` merge when the impression is recorded (a checkpoint has gone out), not only when it is `flushed`, so a `packageInstalled` adoption after a checkpoint sends at once. On CLI exit, `flushAdEngagement` is kicked off before the renderer unmounts the ad cards (so `closeAll` runs against `window_close`, not `unmount`) and its transport is awaited by the bounded remote cleanup. Tests assert checkpoint-once behavior, recorded status until flush, adoption-after-checkpoint sending, and that a throwing or unmounted ad flush never blocks exit.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`, `createEngagementTracker` gains a `markRecordOut()` helper that sets `recordOut` and calls `onRecordOut` once from `sendCheckpoint`, `sendLateClick`, and `flush`; `EngagementTracker` exposes a new `recordOut` getter; `EngagementRegistryEnv` and `createEngagementTracker` options gain `onRecordOut`; and `createEngagementRegistry` threads `onRecordOut` from `status`. In `cli/src/ads/use-ad-engagement.ts`, `adEngagementRegistry` wires `onRecordOut` to `adoption?.mainRecordSent`. In `cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts`, `flushAdEngagement` is started before the renderer teardown (`cleanupLocal`) and awaited within the bounded remote cleanup. In `cli/src/ads/ad-adoption.ts`, the `status` doc and `trySend` now treat recorded as a release state alongside `flushed`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether `onRecordOut` consumers beyond the adoption watcher are registered, or how the `status` API is exposed to the hook or CLI surface.

eli5.text: When you click on an ad inside the Freebuff coding assistant and later install the advertised software, the assistant now reports that adoption to its server as soon as the first record about that ad has been saved, instead of waiting until you close the program. This is internal reliability work for the ad-tracking plumbing (the audience is the Freebuff engineering team), and it does not change what ads you see, what you can install, or how your coding sessions work.

entries.title: CLI cleanup: imprezia-ad and 2 more

ai.title: Drop Imprezia ads and zeroclick provider from ad routing
ai.summary: The Imprezia ad network integration has been fully removed from common, deleting imprezia-ad.ts, imprezia-display.ts, imprezia-trackers.ts and renaming imprezia-viewability.ts to mrc50-viewability.ts. In the CLI ad hook, the `AdProvider` type now only allows 'gravity' or 'first_party', the `impressionIds?` field and the zeroclick impression-endpoint POST were deleted, and zeroclick entries are no longer short-circuited in the choice cache. The ad-experiment module loses the `imprezia_forced`/`imprezia_first` arms entirely, leaving `AdExperimentArm` as just `'control'`, and the corresponding Imprezia fetch-completed event and its sanitizer were stripped from the Axiom operational-log allowlist.
ai.evidence: common/src/util/ad-experiment.ts: removed exports IMPREZIA_EXPERIMENT, isImpreziaAudienceEmail, adExperimentArmForUser, and the ImpreziaAd/ImpreziaTrackers-related schema constants; `AdExperimentArm` type reduced to just 'control'. common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts: deleted ADS_IMPREZIA_FETCH_COMPLETED_EVENT and its sanitizer + allowlisted field set from the event allowlist and switch statement. cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts: removed the 'zeroclick' value from the `AdProvider` type, dropped the `impressionIds?` optional field, removed the `ZEROCLICK_IMPRESSIONS_URL` constant and the zeroclick-specific impression-recording branch, and removed zeroclick short-circuiting in `addToChoiceCache` and the empty-slot fallback check.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show any consumer of the zeroclick or Imprezia constants still reading them, so whether the ad-auction request building in buildAdAuctionRequest silently ignores the removed provider values is not confirmed here.

changes.what: Removed the zeroclick ad provider from the type system and impression tracking, deleting its dedicated impression POST path and choice-cache short-circuit.
Removed Imprezia experiment constants, audience detection, arm-for-user resolver, and reduced AdExperimentArm to only 'control'.
Deleted the ADS_IMPREZIA_FETCH_COMPLETED_EVENT constant and its dedicated sanitizer and allowlisted field definitions from the operational log schema.
Deleted the three Imprezia source files and renamed imprezia-viewability.ts to mrc50-viewability.ts.

eli5.text: The Imprezia ad network has been fully removed from the codebase, along with the zeroclick provider. This means the types of ads that could appear and the code paths used to fetch and display them have been simplified to only two providers now. This change affects internal ad routing and telemetry systems, so if you maintain or operate the Freebuff service, this reduces the ad sources that are supported. For regular users, there is no visible difference in daily use; the assistant still shows ads as before, just from a smaller set of networks.

ai.title: Profile lift experiment telemetry fields removed from ads
ai.summary: The `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` allowlist in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` dropped the `profile_lift_*` block, removing experiment id, epoch id, arm, probability, follow-up timing, maturity, config digest, mode and serving-assignment fields from the `ads.fetch_completed` operational event. Because the allowlist is the sole sieve that decides what survives the content-free operational-event filter before a row enters Axiom, those eleven fields can no longer reach the `ads.fetch_completed` stream. The change accompanies the adjacent rollup of prior ads members on 2026-10-05 and trims experiment telemetry that no longer has a live consumer in the fetch-completed path.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, the `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` allowlist removed the `profile_lift_*` block of fields (`profile_lift_experiment_id`, `profile_lift_epoch_id`, `profile_lift_assignment_version`, `profile_lift_arm`, `profile_lift_arm_probability_ppm`, `profile_lift_followup_start_ms`, `profile_lift_followup_end_ms`, `profile_lift_maturity_at_ms`, `profile_lift_config_digest`, `profile_lift_mode`, `profile_lift_serving_assignment_applied`), so they no longer pass the content-free operational-event filter into the `ads.fetch_completed` stream.
ai.unknowns: The diff and notes do not state which consumer previously read the profile lift fields or whether the underlying experiment module was deleted elsewhere. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

eli5.text: I'll analyze this change for a non-programmer reader. Based on the technical summary and the provided source code context, here's a plain-English explanation of the change: The system operators of the Freebuff service removed eleven pieces of experimental data from a specific operational log that tracks when ad requests are completed. This log acts like a filter - only approved fields make it through to the analytics system, and these experiment-related fields (like experiment ID, arm assignment, and probability scores) are no longer among the approved entries. This change affects only the internal service operators who monitor ad performance and experiment effectiveness. Regular Freebuff users, developers using the CLI, or advertisers won't notice any difference in their daily usage.

ai.title: .gitignore un-ignores browser-runtime dist Next route
ai.summary: The top-level `dist` ignore rule now excludes the directory `freebuff/web/src/app/api/browser-runtime/dist/` via a negated glob, so the Convex HTTP edge proxy's in-repo Next route assets remain tracked. The change corrects repository hygiene for a route that ships source under a `dist` path, and does not affect CLI or web app runtime behavior.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies .gitignore (commit c1286ace) to add a negated glob entry `!freebuff/web/src/app/api/browser-runtime/dist/` alongside the existing `dist` ignore rule, with a comment stating it is a Next route, not build output.
ai.unknowns: The commit introduces no new consumer behavior; the rationale is purely repository hygiene for a Next route whose assets live under a `dist` path.

eli5.text: A maintainer added a single rule to the repository's ignore list so one specific folder of web assets stays tracked in version control. This is purely internal repository housekeeping for a Convex edge route that happens to live under a path normally treated as throwaway build output. It has no effect on Freebuff, Codebuff, or Freebucks accounts, sessions, credits, or daily use, and requires no action from anyone outside the engineering team.
